commands.name: claude-android-qa-plugin:android-emulator-qa-guidance
commands.description: (claude-android-qa-plugin) This skill should be used when validating Android feature flows in an emulator, reproducing Android UI bugs, driving adb input, inspecting uiautomator XML, capturing screenshots, or collecting logcat evidence.

commands.name: claude-android-qa-plugin:android-emulator-qa
commands.description: (claude-android-qa-plugin) Drive Android emulator QA with adb, UI tree inspection, screenshots, and logcat evidence

commands.name: ai-ready-ds:ds-ai-check
commands.description: (AI Ready Design System) Run an AI readiness audit on a Figma design system. Use when the user asks to "check my design system", "audit my DS", "is my design system AI ready", "run ds-ai-check", "check AI readiness", or provides a Figma file URL and wants to know how AI-ready it is. All checks are deterministic and rule-based.

commands.name: animation-studio:animation-studio
commands.description: (animation-studio) This skill should be used when the user asks to "make an animated video about X with music", "make a cartoon / animated short", "animate this story", "make a video like the Opus animations", "make an explainer animation (with a voiceover)", "make a promo video for my app / brand / website", "make an animated Reel / TikTok / Short", "make a lyric video / animate to my song", "make an animated map or infographic", or "make a jingle / birthday video" — a new hand-drawn 2D film where every frame is drawn in code and the soundtrack is synthesized in code (or is the user's own song, beat-analysed), synced from one score, delivered as a 1080p MP4 in 16:9, 9:16, 1:1 or 4:5. Not for CSS/web/UI animation, Lottie/SVG/GIF assets, editing existing video footage, or Remotion/Manim projects.

commands.name: zizi-skills:adversarial-review
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Run several independent model seats against one problem or one plan, make them attack each other, fact-check every contested claim, then ask the human one gate of questions. Two modes: a design panel for an open problem, and a plan review for a drafted or approved plan. Use only when the human asks for adversarial or multi-seat work. Not for a code diff (use /code-review), pure ideation (idea-refine), or a single Verifier pass on one claim.

commands.name: zizi-skills:app-store
commands.description: (zizi-skills) App Store and Google Play listings: title, subtitle, keywords, description, screenshots, previews, ratings prompts. Use when preparing or auditing a store listing or asking why installs are low. Copy wording is plain-language; visuals are design-assets; pricing is marketing.

commands.name: zizi-skills:code-quality
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Standards for reviewing and cleaning up code. Use when reviewing any diff (your own before commit, a Codex or sub-agent diff, a colleague's PR) or when asked to clean up, de-duplicate or delete dead code. Holds the hard rules, the review checklist (standards and spec axes), module-design tests, and proof of deadness before deleting. To run a review use /code-review; to apply cleanups, /simplify.

commands.name: zizi-skills:data-analytics
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Decide which metrics, KPIs and charts an app's data deserves. Use when exploring a schema or domain, planning a dashboard ("what should this show?", "add stats to X"), or choosing which data points matter. Keeps a per-project catalog. Query speed is database-optimization; chart UI is frontend; chart colors are design-guide.

commands.name: zizi-skills:database-optimization
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Correct, fast queries, views, indexes and schema. Use before adding or changing any query (ORM or raw), entity, migration, index or view, and when an endpoint or list is slow. In a TypeORM project, load it before writing ORM code. Which service owns a table is service-architecture; running migrations locally is project-config.

commands.name: zizi-skills:debugging-and-error-recovery
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Root-cause debugging. Use when a test fails, a build breaks, behavior doesn't match expectations, or any unexpected error appears. Builds a loop that goes red on the failure before theorising, ranks falsifiable hypotheses, and ends with a regression test.

commands.name: zizi-skills:deprecation-and-migration
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Remove or replace systems, APIs and features. Use when sunsetting code, migrating users to a new implementation, running a strangler migration off a legacy service, or making an expand/contract schema change while old and new code share one database.

commands.name: zizi-skills:design-assets
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Visual assets: logos, icons, illustrations, hero and OG images, empty-state art, favicons, raster-to-vector conversion. Use whenever a task needs one. Recraft is called first and hand-authoring is the fallback; covers the art-direction brief and integration. Visual judgment is design-guide.

commands.name: zizi-skills:design-guide
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Visual and UX judgment: color, typography, spacing, hierarchy, themes. Use when choosing colors or status/badge colors, theming (white-label included), making a screen "look better" or more polished, or reviewing a UI's visual quality. Decides how it looks; structure is frontend, Tabler specifics are tabler-ui, content placement is information-architecture.

commands.name: zizi-skills:done
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Session close-out with no resume prompt. Use on /done, or when wrapping up a session where nothing remains to resume or the continuation prompt already exists (a standup queue's next item). Runs the handoff close-out minus the resume-prompt step. Need a fresh resume prompt? Use handoff instead, never both. In a parent session it closes the child sessions first.

commands.name: zizi-skills:explain
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Re-explain the last message in plain words, using the project's own vocabulary.

commands.name: zizi-skills:find-skills
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Discover and install agent skills. Use only when the user explicitly asks for a skill ("find or install a skill for X", "is there a skill that..."), never for an ordinary how-do-I question.

commands.name: zizi-skills:first-customers
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Find and reach a product's first customers honestly: demand signals, local-business prospect lists, outreach drafts a human sends. Use when asking "who would buy this" or "how do I get my first users or clients". Offer and positioning are marketing; wording is plain-language.

commands.name: zizi-skills:frontend
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Frontend structure and behavior: components, state, a typed service layer, lists, tables and filters, forms, modals, loading/empty/error states, routing, SSR, web performance. Use when building or refactoring UI or adding any screen. Vue 3 + Tabler today, framework-agnostic in approach. Tabler specifics are tabler-ui; visual judgment is design-guide; content placement is information-architecture.

commands.name: zizi-skills:git-sync
commands.description: (zizi-skills) The standing git workflow. Use at the start of any branch work and before every commit, push, rebase or PR: your own branch (never main), rebased on current main, every branch pushed, PR bodies in the standard shape, PRs reported only when green, and merged branches and worktrees pruned before a session ends.

commands.name: zizi-skills:grant-writing
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Research grant applications: research and mentoring plans, specific aims, budget justifications, abstracts. Use when writing or strengthening a proposal, checking a draft against a funder's guidelines or review criteria, or responding to reviewers. Owns proposal strategy and structure; wording is academic-writing, study design is research-methods.

commands.name: zizi-skills:handoff
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Durable session handoff with a resume prompt. Use when pausing or ending work at a real boundary (a phase or PR done, a blocker, a pivot, a drained queue) or when the user says "hand off" or "we'll continue later". Saves state outside the chat plus an exact resume point, never just a chat summary. No new resume prompt needed? Use done.

commands.name: zizi-skills:i18n
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Multi-language support (i18n/l10n). Use when a task touches a translation file or a user-facing string in a product that ships more than one language: adding a language or key, extracting strings, vue-i18n/nestjs-i18n/go-i18n, locale formatting, translated data (enums, emails, PDFs), locale routing, hreflang, RTL. Its core failure is a key that reaches one pack and not the others.

commands.name: zizi-skills:idea-refine
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Turn a vague idea into a sharp, actionable concept by diverging, then converging. Use for pure ideation: "ideate", "refine this idea", "explore options for X". It sits upstream of a plan; to plan an idea already chosen, use planning.

commands.name: zizi-skills:information-architecture
commands.description: (zizi-skills) How content and pages are organized for their audience: site maps, page inventories, each page's job, where a message or feature lives, navigation and funnels, heading structure, buried or orphaned messages. Applies to docs, books, curricula and papers too. Use when outlining, when adding or reordering pages or sections, and on any content-page review. Looks are design-guide; wording is plain-language or academic-writing.

commands.name: zizi-skills:infrastructure
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Change infrastructure and dev-workflow tooling: Nomad, Consul, Vault, Terraform, Docker, GitHub Actions, task runners, env and direnv setup, setup scripts, a project's own ops CLI, launchd and hooks. Use when editing any of these or debugging env or worktree setup. Looking up how to run a project is project-config; third-party APIs are integrations.

commands.name: zizi-skills:integrations
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Connect to or automate third-party services: REST APIs, MCP servers, OAuth and tokens, webhooks, recurring syncs. Use when building or debugging an integration, scheduling a job against an external service, deciding where automation runs, making external writes idempotent, or researching a vendor API. Internal service-to-service calls are service-architecture.

commands.name: zizi-skills:marketing
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Why people choose, buy, sign up and stay, applied honestly: behavioral models, offers, pricing, trust, urgency, onboarding and growth loops for the apps and sites we build. Use when shaping a landing, pricing, signup or launch page, an offer or free tier, or asking "why would anyone pick this". Wording is plain-language; page structure is information-architecture.

commands.name: zizi-skills:monitoring
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Observability into running code. Use when adding logging or instrumentation, diagnosing a running service ("watch the logs", "what is it actually doing"), standardizing log output, or when a change must be proven on the live app because tests can't reach it. Deploy and alerting stacks are infrastructure; tests are tdd-skill.

commands.name: zizi-skills:orchestration
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Run multi-step or long-running work as an orchestrator over disposable sub-agents. Use at the start of a program phase, migration, broad sweep, deep research or many-file job, or when your context fills with exploration. Not for single-step edits or quick questions.

commands.name: zizi-skills:plain-language
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Clear, friendly, jargon-free writing for non-technical readers: ticket text, QA steps, release notes, status updates, UI copy, business messages. Use when writing for QA, product, stakeholders or end users, or on a "make this less technical" pass. Scholarly prose is academic-writing; document structure is information-architecture.

commands.name: zizi-skills:planning
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Plan before building anything non-trivial: multi-file or multi-phase work, a feature, a migration, or whenever asked to plan. Research, write the plan, ask every decision up front (a second gate only for questions that depend on a first-gate answer), get approval, then execute autonomously. No implementation while the approval gate is open.

commands.name: zizi-skills:project-config
commands.description: (zizi-skills) The recorded facts of how each project runs: node version, env and direnv, package manager, monorepo layout, and the exact install, run, build, test, lint and migrate commands. Consult before your first shell command in a repo and before briefing an agent that will run one. Record any missing fact the moment you find it.

commands.name: zizi-skills:project-manager
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Keep the tracker (Jira, Trello, or GitHub Issues and Projects) in sync with the real work. Use on /project-manager or "file a ticket", "is this tracked", "write QA steps", "audit my tickets", "find duplicates", "clean up the backlog". Drafts every change and asks before writing to the tracker. Working your assigned tickets is standup.

commands.name: zizi-skills:research-methods
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Social and health research design: conceptual and logic models, CBPR/YPAR, participatory and agent-based modeling, spatial indices, implementation frameworks (CFIR, RE-AIM), measures, IRB and human-subjects sections, literature synthesis. Use when planning a study or choosing a method or framework. Proposal structure is grant-writing; wording is academic-writing.

commands.name: zizi-skills:security-and-hardening
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Security standards a default pass gets wrong: credential reach, proving a control holds, leak-free secret scanning, SSRF/TOCTOU, deployment topology. Use when handling untrusted input, auth, sessions, stored data or third-party calls; adding or upgrading a dependency; pinning Actions or base images; editing CI, Dockerfiles or hooks; wiring an MCP server; or when the secret-scan hook denies a commit. Run the review itself with /security-review.

commands.name: zizi-skills:service-architecture
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Backend architecture decisions: service boundaries, splitting vs consolidating, inter-service calls, auth guards and tiers, where logic lives, strangler migrations. Load before adding or versioning an endpoint or a service-to-service call, or deciding which service owns something. Query performance is database-optimization.

commands.name: zizi-skills:source-driven-development
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Ground implementation decisions in official documentation, with citations. Use when building with a framework or library where correctness matters or common patterns may be outdated.

commands.name: zizi-skills:status-update
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Session status as a visual dashboard plus a 2-3 line TLDR, never prose alone. Use on /status-update, "where are we", "what's left", mid-way through a multi-item run, and at any wrap-up covering more than one unit of work.

commands.name: zizi-skills:tabler-ui
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Tabler admin template (tabler.io) components and the workarounds that make them behave in Vue 3. Consult before any Tabler markup or interactive component: modals, dropdowns, badges, grids, forms, icons, wizards, empty states, emails. Structure is frontend; visual judgment is design-guide.

commands.name: zizi-skills:tdd-skill
commands.description: (zizi-skills) Test-first (red-green-refactor) for any codebase. Use when adding or changing behavior, fixing a bug (it starts with a failing regression test), or asked to add or cover tests. Finds how this project runs tests, names the seams under test, and verifies on a live stack when a unit test can't reach the behavior. Watching an existing change run is /verify.

commands.name: desktop-commander:ai-tools-setup
commands.description: (Desktop Commander) Set up, connect, validate, and repair Claude Desktop and MCP servers using Desktop Commander — inspecting and fixing mcp.json / claude_desktop_config.json, getting MCP servers to connect, and diagnosing local AI tooling. Use when a user wants to install, configure, connect, validate, or fix Claude Desktop, an MCP server, an MCP config file, or a local AI agent/gateway. Trigger on the symptoms that actually bring people in: "Claude can't see my tools", "my MCP server isn't showing up", "tools aren't loading in Claude", "add an MCP server", "my MCP isn't connecting", "fix my Claude Desktop config", "the agent won't respond", "wire up Ollama / LM Studio", "restart Claude Desktop". Also covers local agent gateways like OpenClaw and Hermes.

commands.name: desktop-commander:computer-health-check
commands.description: (Desktop Commander) Run a comprehensive, read-only health check on the user's computer and return a scored chat summary with prioritized, plain-English recommendations and safe cleanup suggestions. Use this whenever the user wants to check their computer's health, speed it up, free up / reclaim disk space, find what's eating CPU / memory / storage, check battery health and wear, audit login & startup items, see pending updates, or asks for a "tune-up", "checkup", "system report", "health check", or "is my Mac/PC/laptop healthy". Trigger even on casual phrasing like "my laptop feels slow", "why is my fan so loud", "my computer is laggy", "running out of space", or "clean up my machine". Works on macOS, Windows, and Linux. This is a Desktop Commander skill: it relies on a real local shell (start_process / interact_with_process) and is strictly read-only by default — it never needs sudo and only performs cleanups the user explicitly approves.

commands.name: desktop-commander:desktop-commander-overview
commands.description: (Desktop Commander) Use for Desktop Commander MCP capabilities — persistent shells and REPLs, long-running processes, filesystem beyond the workspace, structured files (.xlsx, .docx, .pdf, images) and large local data files such as CSVs, ripgrep search at scale, SSH, or cross-turn state.

commands.name: desktop-commander:knowledge-base
commands.description: (Desktop Commander) Create and maintain a Markdown knowledge base that any AI agent can read, search, and update. Use when the user wants to start a knowledge base, add or update notes, organize docs/notes for an agent or LLM to consume, build an index of notes, or run a cleanup/maintenance pass on an existing MD knowledge base. Triggers include "knowledge base", "KB", "notes for the agent", "index of notes", "second brain", "docs for AI context", "add a note", "update the KB".

commands.name: desktop-commander:obsidian-vault
commands.description: (Desktop Commander) Organize Obsidian vaults with MOCs, wikilinks, frontmatter/properties, dashboards, orphan-note checks, and cleanup workflows. Use ONLY when the user explicitly refers to Obsidian — by naming "Obsidian", an Obsidian "vault", or an Obsidian-specific feature such as wikilinks ("[[ ]]"), the Dataview or Bases plugins, or Obsidian Properties. Within that Obsidian context it covers creating Maps of Content, adding/fixing wikilinks, finding orphan notes, normalizing YAML frontmatter, generating Dataview/Bases dashboards, organizing folders, deduplicating or renaming notes, and preparing the vault for AI use. Do NOT use this skill for generic note-taking, Markdown, or knowledge-base requests that don't mention Obsidian.

commands.name: desktop-commander:terminal
commands.description: (Desktop Commander) Use Desktop Commander for terminal and command-line work, especially anything that needs a shell whose state persists across turns: Python/Node REPLs, database shells, dev servers and other long-running processes, SSH into remote machines, and Windows PowerShell. Also handles everyday terminal tasks — navigating folders, choosing the right command for the user's shell (PowerShell, cmd, bash, zsh), running Docker/curl/cloud-CLI commands, inspecting processes and ports, and saving recurring workflows as scripts — even when the user doesn't say "Desktop Commander" or "terminal." Reach for it on pasted errors like "command not found", "permission denied", "EADDRINUSE", "address already in use", "npm ERR!", "ModuleNotFoundError", or "ENOENT", and on intents like "what's using port 3000", "kill that process", "ssh into my server", or "why won't my dev server start". Works on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Never run destructive commands without explicit confirmation.

commands.name: canva:canva-brand-check
commands.description: (canva) Check a Canva design against a brand kit and report where it diverges — off-palette colors, non-brand fonts, logo misuse, and off-tone copy. Read-only; makes no changes. Use when the user asks "is this on brand", "check this against our brand kit", "do a brand review", "does this match our brand guidelines", or "brand-check my design".

commands.name: canva:canva-bulk-create
commands.description: (canva) Bulk-create Canva designs from tabular data using a brand template with autofill fields, producing one design per row. Use when users say "bulk create designs from this CSV", "generate one design per row", "create a design for each product", "batch generate from a template", or "autofill a template from a spreadsheet". Accepts any tabular data source — uploaded files, pasted tables, JSON, or URLs.

commands.name: canva:canva-cli
commands.description: (canva) Use the Canva CLI (`canva api`) for Canva REST API workflows with local files, scripts, and coding agents. Use when the request needs direct, programmatic work with Canva designs, folders, assets, exports, or other REST API resources.

commands.name: canva:canva-edit-design
commands.description: (canva) Make edits to an existing Canva design — change or fix text, replace/insert/delete images and videos, reformat text (size, weight, style, color, alignment, lists, line height), reposition or resize elements, and update the title. Use when the user wants to change, edit, update, fix, translate, replace, or reformat content in a specific Canva design. This is the safe edit engine that other Canva skills (e.g. implement-feedback) build on.

commands.name: canva:canva-design-feedback
commands.description: (canva) Read a Canva design and return structured, actionable design feedback — visual hierarchy, copy/messaging, layout & spacing, consistency, readability, and accessibility. Read-only; makes no changes to the design. Use when the user asks to "review my design", "give me feedback on this", "critique my deck/poster/flyer", "how can I improve this design", or "what's wrong with this slide".

commands.name: canva:canva-implement-feedback
commands.description: (canva) Implement reviewer feedback on a Canva design. Reads all comment threads, synthesises what reviewers want, makes the clear-cut changes directly, and flags anything that needs a human decision. Use when the user asks to "implement feedback on my deck", "address comments on a design", "apply review feedback", "fix the comments on my presentation", or "implement the feedback".

commands.name: canva:canva-resize-for-social-media
commands.description: (canva) Resize a Canva design into multiple social media formats (Facebook post, Facebook story, Instagram post, Instagram story, LinkedIn post). Use this skill when users want to resize Canva designs specifically for multiple social media platforms in one operation, rather than resizing to a single format manually.

commands.name: ecom:ecom-landing-pages
commands.description: (ecom) Use when someone wants landing page ideas, concepts, or angles for a store: "give me landing page concepts", "LP ideas", "landing page angles", a campaign or ad landing page, pages for a new audience/segment, a seasonal/event/promo page, or a geo/local page. Also use when a chosen concept gets picked and needs building out into an actual page (section-by-section blueprint), or when auditing an existing landing page against best practice. The core insight: one product becomes dozens of pages by varying the ANGLE, not the product. Not for full-site information architecture, product detail pages, collection pages, or blog/SEO content (a landing page has ONE goal, no site chrome). Use an SEO/content skill. Not for the ad or email creative itself, though message match with the page matters.

commands.name: ecom:shopify-alt-text

The page reads the CRM itself through a read-only grant, so it refreshes whenever a viewer opens it.
